reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the formation of a composite amorphous/nanocrystalline structure and improved corrosion resistance in PWR water for AlNbTiZr coatings, but it does not address Cr–Zr interdiffusion, high-temperature steam oxidation, or the proposed diffusion-barrier mechanism, leaving most key premises unsupported.
premises: AlNbTiZr MEA coating forms a composite amorphous/nanocrystalline bcc structure that creates a dense oxide and diffusion barrier
Incorporation of Al and Nb promotes a stable, protective oxide layer and enhances metallurgical bonding with Zr substrate
Multi-element lattice distortion increases activation energy for atomic diffusion, reducing Cr and Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures
The coating provides robust corrosion/oxidation protection under PWR water and high-temperature steam
The coating suppresses Cr–Zr interdiffusion, preventing premature failure seen in pure Cr coatings
